title: An algebraic approach to product-form stationary distributions for some reaction networks: the kernel of the reduced matrix is one-dimensional over the field of fractions
author: Beatriz Pascual-Escudero; Linard Hoessly
work: An algebraic approach to product-form stationary distributions for some reaction networks
difficulty_reason: Counted unit: the article's Corollary (source0.tex lines 502--504, source label clm2): under the article's linearity assumption on the transition intensities, the kernel of the reduced matrix is spanned by a unique vector of homogeneous polynomials in the reaction-rate parameters, up to multiplication by a non-zero constant; delivered with the article's complete original proof at source0.tex lines 506--538 (one adjacent proof environment of 33 lines that opens and closes inside the retained span). The proof is complete and closed inside the retained span together with its retained context: it uses the retained rank lemma over the field of fractions to know that the kernel is one-dimensional, parametrises the kernel vector by the minors of the reduced matrix, verifies that these minors are homogeneous polynomials of the same degree in the rate parameters, checks the support conditions enumerated in the proof, and concludes that the resulting vector is unique up to scaling. The corollary is the algebraic step that makes the article's parametrisation of steady states of reaction networks well defined. H2: a research-level algebraic-statistics corollary whose proof combines rank arguments over a field of fractions, minor parametrisations of a one-dimensional kernel and homogeneity and support checks; it is well beyond ordinary PhD qualifying exercises.
